title: Bus Speed Race
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Communication Buses
I2C
SPI
UART
Frame Rate
description: Compare how long UART, I2C and SPI take to send one full screen of pixels to three different displays, on a logarithmic time axis.

learningObjectives: Compare the time UART, I2C and SPI need to send one frame to a display
Calculate frame time from bytes, bits per byte and bus speed
Evaluate which bus a display needs to reach 20 frames per second
prerequisites: Bits, bytes and the I2C, SPI and UART buses (Chapter 8)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Comparison of two strategies on the same data
keyQuestions: Why does the UART bar not change when you move either slider?
How many times more data does the 240x240 color frame hold than the OLED frame?
What clock speed does I2C need to send a color frame at 20 fps, and is that possible?
commonMisconceptions: A faster bus always matters (for a 1,024-byte OLED, 400 kHz I2C is already fast enough for a clock)
Doubling resolution doubles the data (doubling width and height makes four times the pixels)
assessmentOpportunities: The student computes 1,024 x 9 / 400,000 = 23 ms for the OLED on 400 kHz I2C.
The student explains that each tick on a log axis is ten times the previous one.
The student justifies a bus choice using frames per second, not just "faster".

controls.label: Display
controls.description: Chooses the 128x64 mono OLED, 240x240 color or 320x240 color frame size
